job.title: ACCOUNT EXECUTIVE
job.description:
• Pioneer in sleep technology for over a century
  • Ongoing training and career advancement opportunities
  • A culture that prioritises well-being 


About the organisation

Sealy of Australia are the market-leading manufacturer of premium sleeping solutions throughout Australia and the Asia Pacific. In business since 1923, Sealy partners with their national network of retailers to help millions of people achieve better sleep. Their pursuit to refine and advance Posturepedic® technology backed by orthopaedic research has resulted in world–class innovation that people love. Headquartered in Brisbane with six manufacturing plants across Australia and New Zealand, staffed by over 750 highly-skilled, highly valued employees, Sealy have a passion for developing local expertise and talent. 


About the role

Based in Melbourne and reporting to the Victorian Sales and Operations Manager, the Account Executive will execute sales strategies to drive long-term market share, sales, and profit growth across Victoria and Tasmania. The appointee will be responsible for developing and managing major accounts by strengthening key relationships with specialist retail partners. This role is part of an established and highly productive team, with a collaborative and collegiate culture and will play a critical in supporting Sealy’s growth strategy over the next 3–5 years.


About you

With prior experience as an Account Executive in high-end consumer products, you are a proactive and customer-focused professional with exceptional communication and relationship-building skills. You have a deep understanding of the ultra-premium wholesale industry selling into a reputable retail customer base and a proven ability to foster genuine relationships with key accounts to drive their success. Working autonomously within a team environment, you bring strong strategic, commercial, and analytical skills. Comfortable traveling across Victoria and Tasmania, you are highly motivated to contribute to both key account growth and your own career development.


How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV. For more information prior to application, please contact Charlie Hess at SHK via email on Charlie.hess@shk.com.au quoting reference 3670676. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.

job.title: IMPLEMENTATION MANAGER
job.description:
• Lead program establishment internally and with partner networks
  • Deliver high-accountability government-funded initiatives
  • Partner directly with a vision-led CEO


About the organisation

Our client is a well-established organisation working across housing, legal assistance and services, and advocacy. They provide hands-on support, advice, and education, with a clear focus on making the housing system fairer so people can live in safe, secure, and affordable homes. After a period of significant growth, the organisation has secured multi-year government funding to design and deliver a substantially expanded model of service across the state. The work involves building integrated frontline and specialist capability, with the organisation playing a central role in the new arrangements. There is no template for this. It is a genuine build, and the appointee will be shaping the model as it is delivered.


About the role

Reporting to the CEO, the Implementation Manager leads the establishment of the organisation's funded service components within a new statewide service model. The broader program framework, funding requirements and implementation parameters are established externally, while the organisation is responsible for delivering its own services, systems, workforce and operational readiness. They will also coordinate with government and external partner agencies where required to meet program guidelines, resolve shared dependencies and deliver agreed service interfaces. This is not a pre-packaged rollout. Many decisions are still open and will be resolved progressively, and the role exists to bring them to resolution and keep the build moving. The Implementation Manager, working with the SLT, owns the implementation plan, milestones, dependencies, decision records, and readiness reporting.. With the CEO focused outward on government and funder relationships, this role works with SLT to ensure delivery. Success requires disciplined delivery, clear decision making and sustained momentum across internal teams while managing dependencies with external partners. Fixed-term contract (12–18 months).


About you

You bring demonstrated experience coordinating complex projects, service implementations or organisational change initiatives across multiple teams and stakeholders. Change management is your strong suit, and you have strong project governance expertise in milestone tracking, budget monitoring, risk and issue management, and senior-level reporting. You are comfortable building something new, familiar with ambiguity, emergence and iterative decision-making. Collaborative and relationship-driven, you are able to influence without formal authority and to adapt as external dependencies evolve. You are a strong communicator who knows when to push for a decision and when to give people room, and you are able to manage upward effectively, supporting clear priorities, timely decisions and disciplined follow-through in a fast-moving executive environment. Experience gained in a larger organisation across government, higher education, not-for-profit/community services, or similar would position you well to build structure in a more agile environment. A relevant qualification, along with a current Police Check and Working with Children Check, is required.


How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV. For more information prior to application, please contact Evan Willen at SHK via email on evan.willen@shk.com.au, quoting reference 3663240. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK. Applications close 27 September 11:59pm.

job.title: ASSOCIATE DIRECTOR, MARKETING
job.description:
• Leading Victorian university
  • Strategic leadership of international and domestic marketing
  • Agile and emerging technology focus


About the organisation

A long-established Australian university with an extensive multi-campus footprint, this institution offers a fully integrated pathway from vocational education through to higher education. Distinguished by a progressive approach to teaching and learning, it is driven by a clear and compelling purpose: to make a real difference to the lives of its students and the communities it serves. As a leading provider to first-in-family students, the university has carved out a distinctive and meaningful position in the Australian higher education landscape - one its people believe in deeply. World-class education and facilities underpin a student experience that reflects the institution's commitment to access, equity, and excellence.


About the role

Reporting to the Director, Marketing, Communications and Growth, the Associate Director, Marketing provides strategic leadership for the University's integrated marketing function, ensuring marketing strategy, brand positioning and market engagement support the institution’s strategic objectives, growth agenda and reputation. Driving a high performance team in an Agile environment, the appointee will develop the enterprise-wide marketing strategy, oversee marketing capability and governance frameworks, and drive evidence-based decision making across domestic and international markets. The role provides leadership across brand strategy, marketing planning, digital marketing, campaign optimisation, market intelligence and organisational capability, working collaboratively with executive leaders, academic institutes and professional services to enhance student acquisition, engagement and reputation. Key to success will be a firm grasp of emerging technology, including AI and generative AI, and evolving channels.


About you

You are a contemporary marketing leader with best-practice expertise and a genuine understanding of how emerging technology, including AI, is reshaping audience behavior. With experience navigating large complex service organisations, you possess demonstrated success leading enterprise marketing strategy and integrated marketing initiatives that deliver measurable outcomes. You are adept at advising senior executives, influencing organisational decision-making, and building productive internal and external stakeholder relationships. Your track record leading multidisciplinary teams in Agile ways of working includes building capability, driving performance and leading transformational change. Underpinning your deep experience in brand strategy, CX, market positioning, and use of market intelligence and analytics to inform strategy, are your strong commercial acumen, passion to make a difference and a belief in the power of education to change lives.


How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV. For more information prior to application, please contact Dalia Klein at SHK on 0401 000 499 quoting reference 3661033. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK. Applications close 11.30pm Friday 25 September.

job.title: CHIEF RISK OFFICER, EPA VICTORIA
job.description:
• Victoria's independent environmental regulator
  • Embedding risk-based regulation to protect public and environmental health
  • Strategic risk leadership through the organisation’s next chapter


About the organisation

Environment Protection Authority Victoria (EPA) is the state's environmental regulator, working to prevent and reduce the harmful effects of pollution and waste on Victorian communities and ecosystems. Operating under a strong legislative mandate and a science-based approach, EPA partners with government, industry and the public to protect the environment and human health. This organisation is values-led, future-focused, and committed to delivering lasting impact for all Victorians.


About the role

Reporting to the CEO, the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) will establish and lead EPA Victoria’s new Risk, Assurance and Integrity Division, bringing together assurance, complaints, integrity and risk functions into a high-performing capability. The CRO will provide strategic leadership across regulatory and enterprise risk, oversee assurance and audit activities, and serve as a trusted adviser to the Minister, Board, CEO and Executive. Responsible for building EPA Victoria's regulatory risk framework including developing risk appetite, sector and site risk profiles, prioritisation tools, escalation pathways and decision rights, the CRO ensures that scarce regulatory resources are directed toward the areas of greatest public and environmental impact. A key priority will be driving organisation-wide

cultural change, embedding risk-based decision-making and building the systems, frameworks and capability that strengthens regulatory effectiveness.


About you

You are an accomplished risk or regulatory leader with experience operating in complex public sector, statutory or regulatory environments. You have led significant risk maturity and organisational change initiatives, building capability, influencing culture and embedding risk-based decision-making across large organisations. A trusted and credible stakeholder leader, you provide clear advice at board, executive and ministerial levels, engage confidently with industry and regulatory partners, and bring the resilience, judgement and political acumen to drive change in complex and contested environments. A relevant tertiary qualification is desirable, as is professional accreditation in risk management, assurance, regulatory practice or governance. Above all, you are driven by the opportunity to make a tangible impact through effective, risk-based regulation that protects the environment and the Victorian community.


How to apply

For more information, please review the Candidate Brief, then click ‘apply now’ above to submit your CV/resume and a concise cover letter. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK. Closes 16 September.

job.title: FINANCIAL CONTROLLER
job.description:
• Lead and elevate the finance team
  • Premier Australian commercial law firm
  • Underpin firm-wide financial integrity


About the organisation

The organisation is a premier Australian commercial law firm with offices in Melbourne and Sydney. It provides strategic legal and commercial advice to a diverse range of Australian and international corporations, high-net-worth individuals and large family businesses. The firm is regularly involved in landmark transactions and is known for its innovative, commercially focused advice. It is widely regarded within the profession as a high-performing firm, a quality that permeates every function, not only its legal teams. 


About the role

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Financial Controller leads and elevates the firm's financial management function. The role oversees financial and accounting operations, including financial reporting and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, cost control, working capital, trust management, payroll and compliance. The Financial Controller partners with the CFO on financial insights into client, matter and departmental profitability, and delivers accurate day-one monthly results. The role leads a team of five, spanning payroll, accounts payable, trust and the general ledger, and is responsible for developing that team and driving a high-performance culture. The Financial Controller will also contribute to process improvement, automation and finance projects across the firm. Key to success will be ensuring the common things are done uncommonly well: accurate, trusted and reliable financial operations that the firm can depend on.


About you

CA qualified, you have 10+ years of experience in accounting or finance, including at least five years in a leadership role, ideally from within a legal or professional services environment. You bring strong technical knowledge of accounting, tax and compliance requirements for partnerships and trusts, and are a personable leader who sets clear expectations, works collaboratively, and develops those reporting to you. You communicate well, hold high work standards, and are calm under pressure, ensuring a high standard of accuracy and tight deadlines are met. You are highly organised, commercially minded, and able to interpret what stakeholders are truly asking for and add value to the process. You are confident to challenge the status quo, and you bring a genuine interest in improving processes through technology and automation.


How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV along with a covering letter. For more information prior to application, please contact Andrea Ogden at SHK on 0448 008 630 or via email on andrea.ogden@shk.com.au, quoting reference #3662658. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.﻿

job.title: E-COMMERCE & GROWTH MANAGER
job.description:
• Own a seven-figure marketing budget
  • Vertically integrated, Australian apparel business
  • Drive full-price e-commerce growth across retail and wholesale


About the organisation

This privately owned Australian apparel business has been operating for approximately twenty years. It designs, manufactures, wholesales and retails entirely under company-owned brands — simultaneously and at scale. The wholesale arm supplies around 350 boutique stockists across Australia and New Zealand; through its retail network that spans approximately twenty bricks-and-mortar stores. Both channels are supported by e-commerce dot-coms and underpinned by a bespoke, real-time inventory management system that integrates across all channels simultaneously. The business is lean, fast-moving, operating from Melbourne's outer eastern suburbs.


About the role

Reporting to the owner-operator, the E-commerce & Growth Manager takes end-to-end ownership of digital marketing strategy across e-commerce, bricks-and-mortar retail, and wholesale channels. The role is trusted with a seven-figure annual marketing budget and will begin with a thorough audit of current spend across Meta, Google, Google Merchant Centre, affiliates, and influencer partnerships. The appointee will be review, assess and identify what is generating an adequate return on investment and rebuild channel strategies accordingly. A core priority is developing separate, data-led strategies for channels that are currently inconsistent and have significantly greater potential. The role owns Meta campaigns at the most senior level, takes direct responsibility for Google and Google Merchant Centre management, brings rigour to influencer and affiliate activity, and develops currently underutilised channels including TikTok, YouTube, and emerging website-integrated tools. The role manages two existing marketing team members and will be a senior member of this thriving and ambitious business. 


About you

You are a senior digital marketer with genuine omnichannel experience spanning both e-commerce and physical retail. Your Meta expertise is extensive and you are hands-on. You have owned high-value campaigns at the most senior level and are fluent in the Meta Business Manager ecosystem, including managing AI overrides, ad structures, and attribution. You are equally capable across Google Ads, Google Merchant Centre, and SEO fundamentals, and comfortable managing or directing third parties across these channels. Analytically strong, you pull insights from data, build evidence-based strategies, and can articulate clearly what is working and why. Experience in fashion, apparel, or comparable retail is highly desirable. You thrive in flat, fast-paced, owner-operated environments, communicate directly, and are comfortable being on-site as a dynamic leader in this team.


How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV. For more information prior to application, please contact Kylie Kilmartin at SHK on 0401 167 433 or via email kylie.kilmartin@shk.com.au. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.

job.title: EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR, GLOBAL RESILIENCE
job.description:
• Australia's largest and most international university
  • Establish and lead the global security risk function
  • Protect research integrity and institutional resilience


About the organisation

With a footprint that extends across Australia, Malaysia, Indonesia, Italy, China and India, and comprising more than 20,000 staff and approximately 86,000 students globally, Monash University is Australia’s largest and most international university. In its short history, Monash has rapidly risen through global university rankings and firmly established itself among the world's best universities. Change has been the driving force of Monash’s growth and success, and it’s the foundation of the future as Monash redefines what it means to be a university. Deeply committed to the transformative power of education and research, Monash shapes the future through excellent and immersive education and purposeful research focused on addressing today’s global challenges.


About the role

Reporting to the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (International) and Senior Vice-President, and with a dotted reporting line to Monash’s Vice-Chancellor and President, the Executive Director, Global Resilience is a newly created executive appointment responsible for establishing and leading Monash's central global security and resilience function. The role will provide strategic leadership and coordination across the Monash Group, including international campuses, controlled entities, and institutional partnerships for the identification, assessment, and mitigation of complex global security risks, including foreign interference, research security and personnel-related risks. This encompasses optimising the management and strengthening staff awareness of these risks, and leading policy and process changes. The position will carry institutional accountability for the quality and consistency of global security risk assessments conducted across the Group, and provide authoritative advice and assurance to the University Council and its Risk and Audit Committee, the Vice-Chancellor and senior leadership on emerging and sensitive global security matters. The appointee will serve as Monash's primary interface with national security agencies and government bodies, including ASIO, DFAT and Home Affairs, and will chair the newly established Global Risk Advisory Group. In establishing a community of practice for global security risk and resilience, and leading a small team, the Executive Director will inspire high performance and drive organisational change.


About you

You are a senior executive with deep experience in a large, complex organisation with international operations in higher education, research, government or a closely adjacent sector. This includes a sophisticated understanding of how a research-intensive university functions, including the dynamics of international research collaboration, transnational education and researcher-to-researcher engagement. An Australian citizen, your background gives you genuine expertise in one or more of the following domains: national security, foreign policy, research security or international relations. International and multi-jurisdictional experience and exposure, and nuanced insights into geopolitics most relevant to the University, will be highly regarded. You are adept at operating across decentralised environments, exercising lateral influence without direct authority, and engaging credibly with discerning senior internal and stakeholders with diverse perspectives. Applying your judgement under pressure, precision and economy of communication and exceptional influencing skills, you are comfortable advising on matters with no clear right answer, synthesising complex intelligence, and making or enabling consequential decisions with speed and discretion. Adept at moving between strategic advisory responsibilities and hands-on operational engagement, you are motivated by the opportunity to enhance critical capability for an institution that shapes the future.


How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV along with a covering letter. For more information prior to application, please contact David Pleydell at SHK via email on david.pleydell@shk.com.au, quoting reference 3652034. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.

job.title: BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT MANAGER - NSW
job.description:
• Take ownership of NSW for a well-established Australian business
  • Strong existing client base with significant growth potential
  • Autonomous role with significant career opportunity


About the organisation

Our client is a highly successful Australian owned business with a history spanning more than 50 years supporting the commercial and industrial property sector. The organisation delivers specialist project services across warehouse, industrial, office and commercial environments partnering with property owners, occupiers and developers to deliver complex projects. With a strong reputation built on quality, service and long-standing client relationships, the business continues to experience sustained demand across Australia. New South Wales is already one of the organisation's largest and most important markets and represents a significant opportunity for future growth.


About the role

The Business Development Manager NSW will be responsible for driving revenue growth and strengthening the organisation's presence across the state. This strategically important appointment presents an opportunity to take ownership of an established territory with strong existing revenue, a recognised market reputation and substantial further potential. Working closely with operational and leadership teams, you will focus on building strategic relationships, expanding existing customer engagement and developing new business opportunities across the commercial property, industrial, warehousing and logistics sectors. Success will come through developing trusted relationships with property owners, asset managers, institutional property groups, leasing agents, developers and other key stakeholders involved in industrial and commercial property projects. This is a highly autonomous position offering the opportunity to establish a strong local presence, become a recognised face of the business across New South Wales and play a key role in the next phase of growth.

 

About you

You are an experienced business development professional with a proven track record of generating new business and growing revenue within the commercial property, industrial, logistics, construction services or related sectors. You bring an established network across the NSW market and are confident engaging with property owners, asset managers, leasing agents, developers, occupiers and other key industry stakeholders. A natural relationship builder, you have demonstrated success identifying opportunities, influencing decision makers and managing long sales cycles through to conversion. You are commercially astute, self-motivated and comfortable operating autonomously while maintaining strong collaboration with internal teams. You are confident in taking ownership of a strategically important market, building upon an already successful business presence and playing a leading role in driving the next phase of growth.


How to apply

job.title: HEAD OF CUSTOMER OPERATIONS
job.description:
• Industry leading national service organisation
  • Centralise and modernise customer operations at scale
  • Shape the future of a company entering its next phase of growth


About the organisation

This trusted national services organisation represents prominent brands across the country. Operating across both consumer and business customers, it is embarking on a significant transformation agenda to modernise operations, improve customer outcomes and position the organisation for long-term growth. Backed by an engaged executive team and a clear strategic vision, this employer offers a genuine opportunity to influence significant change and growth. The working environment is agile and commercial, empowering its leaders to make decisions and shape outcomes that positively impact millions of customers around the country.


About the role

Reporting to the Chief Customer Officer, the Head of Customer Operations will lead the transformation and integration of several operational functions. With responsibility for the end-to-end delivery of integrated operational and billing services, the role will focus on connecting people, processes and systems to create a more efficient, scalable and customer-centric operating environment. Covering areas including customer operations, billing, invoicing, supplier performance and service delivery support, the role will drive improvements across systems, processes, governance and operating practices to enhance service delivery, reduce duplication and support consistent outcomes across the organisation. With the opportunity to build a more unified and future-ready function, success will be measured by operational excellence, enhanced customer outcomes, strong partner performance, revenue integrity and commercial outcomes. Automation, digitisation and AI will be key pillars of the transformation agenda, making this an outstanding opportunity to play a leading role in one of the organisation's most significant change programs while shaping a more connected, data-driven and future-ready operating model.

 

About you

You are an experienced operational transformation leader of customer functions, with a track record of improving large-scale, customer-centric service environments supporting significant and complex service delivery ecosystems. You have successfully led the delivery of integrated operational and billing services, including developing and executing operational and billing strategies, working across multiple internal stakeholder groups to redesign operating models, and implementing process improvements, leveraging technology, data and automation to deliver measurable customer, commercial and business outcomes. Customer focused by nature, you understand how operational excellence, governance, controls, revenue integrity and scalable processes combine to create outstanding service outcomes. Comfortable operating in ambiguity, you combine best practice structure, sophistication and change capability, with the agility and pragmatism required to lead transformation, manage complexity and drive performance in an evolving environment. You are highly customer-centric, motivated by the opportunity to build capability, challenge existing ways of working and deliver lasting organisational impact.

job.title: HEAD OF MARKETING & PARTNERSHIPS
job.description:
• Trusted motoring services organisation backed by high profile brands
  • Drive B2B and B2C customer engagement, CX and commercial outcomes
  • Support exciting new future strategy and vision


About the organisation

This organisation provides critical B2B and B2C customer services and rewards across Australia. With a vision to continue to support millions of customers now and in the future, the organisation has launched a new strategy integrating its services through leveraging data, digital and AI capabilities. Drawing on unique national strengths across its services, and responding to a market where integrated solutions and digital-first experiences are increasingly critical, it will deliver a clearer customer proposition, stronger unified brand, deeper customer relationships, and customer experiences that are simpler, more connected and more valuable.


About the role

Reporting to the Chief Customer Officer and leading a small team, the Head of Marketing & Club Partnerships will develop and deliver B2B and B2C marketing and partnership initiatives that drive customer growth, engagement and commercial outcomes. The role is accountable for brand and campaign performance, customer insights, partner relationships and customer value proposition development. This includes managing brand strategy, ensuring a consistent and differentiated market position, integrated marketing strategies that drive customer acquisition, retention, engagement and revenue growth, leveraging customer and market insights to identify growth opportunities, and leading strategic partner relationships. The appointee will collaborate with stakeholders across the organisation and ensure a consistent customer proposition, data-driven decision making, and a simplified, customer-centric operating model that delivers value for customers, partners and the organisation.


About you

You are a customer centric B2B and B2C marketing and partner leader, with experience in best practice service organisations, driving change and transformation. Experience in the EV, energy or automotive sector is advantageous. With the ability to inspire, develop and empower a high-performing team, you are a strategic thinker, passionate about understanding customer needs and highly commercial. Adept at flexing and working in dynamic environments, you are in sync with growth drivers, revenue generation, ROI and business performance. Underpinning your best practice marketing pedigree, is your proven ability to establish and maintain trusted relationships with partners, senior stakeholders, and industry, influence outcomes and align diverse stakeholders, lead organisational change, challenge existing practices, and drive continuous improvement using customer insights, market intelligence and data to inform decisions and measure success. Your drive for results and passion for the customer, will see you thrive in this transformational marketing opportunity, enhancing customer value, strengthening partnerships, and driving commercial growth.


How to apply

job.title: MANAGER, PHILANTHROPY
job.description:
• One of Australia's most trusted charities
  • Lead a national major gifts team
  • Exciting transformational growth mandate


About the organisation

This organisation is one of Australia's most recognised and trusted charities operating nationally across every state and territory. With a broad footprint spanning social services, community support, and emergency relief, its operations touch every demographic and age group while also bringing hope to people experiencing hardship and injustice. The organisation serves people across all walks of life — from crisis support to long-term community development. A substantial fundraising operation, underpinned by a high-performing transformational giving team, has delivered consistent year-on-year growth and continues to play a critical role in advancing the organisation’s purpose. Through an integrated and holistic approach, it creates lasting spiritual and social change for individuals and families across Australia.


About the role

Reporting to the General Manager, Transformational Gifts, the Manager, Philanthropy plays a critical leadership role in advancing the organisation’s mission through the development of meaningful, high-value philanthropic relationships in line with the fundraising strategy. This position is responsible for driving sustainable income growth by identifying, cultivating, soliciting and stewarding major donors including securing seven-figure gifts, and building strong, long-term relationships with philanthropic stakeholders. Combining strategic thinking with hands-on relationship management, the appointee will ensure that philanthropic investment is aligned with organisational priorities and delivers measurable social impact. Collaborating with internal stakeholders to translate programmatic needs into compelling funding propositions, the appointee will build long-term partnerships grounded in trust, transparency and shared purpose, and through disciplined pipeline management, strong market intelligence, and exceptional donor engagement, contribute, to revenue diversification, multi-year funding security, and the overall growth of the philanthropy portfolio. The role is also responsible for achieving financial and non-financial targets, inspiring a national team that is tasked with acquiring new strategic relationships, and driving revenue growth and retention. Critical to success is building team capabilities and optimising ROI performance, while ensuring contemporary best practice processes. 


About you

You are an experienced philanthropy or major gifts leader with demonstrable experience securing seven-figure gifts. You bring leadership experience, ideally across a geographically dispersed team, and possess the commercial and strategic capability to manage a multi ten-million-dollar portfolio of philanthropic revenue. Your stakeholder management skills are well developed, and you present with the gravitas and executive presence required to engage ultra-high-net-worth individuals and their intermediaries. You have the ability to navigate a large complex organisation and to work collaboratively and collectively with this framework. You may come from a large charity, higher education, health or medical research, other relevant philanthropic sectors, or a high-net-worth relationship management background in wealth or private banking where your skills translate meaningfully into the welfare sector. You thrive on operating within a values-led, mission-driven organisation where you can meaningfully impact and transform people’s lives.

job.title: GENERAL MANAGER, TECHNOLOGY
job.description:
• Enterprise technology roadmap delivery
  • Victorian transport accident insurer
  • Enabling better outcomes for injured Victorians


About the organisation

The Transport Accident Commission (TAC) is a Victorian Government-owned organisation responsible for managing the transport accident scheme, providing support and compensation to those injured in transport accidents. The TAC operates across a significant portfolio of services, with a focus on improving the lives of those affected by transport accidents and contributing to road safety more broadly. Headquartered in Geelong, the organisation is undergoing a period of sustained enterprise transformation, with technology at the centre of its strategic agenda.


About the role

Reporting to the Executive General Manager, Enterprise Transformation, the General Manager, Technology leads the Information, Digital and Technology Branch—including shared Technology Operations with WorkSafe Victoria—overseeing approximately 100 staff. The role carries accountability for delivering and maintaining the Enterprise Technology Roadmap, migrating legacy systems to future-state platforms, managing the full technology lifecycle, and leading the TAC's cyber security capability. The GM Technology will oversee technology operations, ensuring a stable and seamless environment for the TAC, its clients, and key stakeholders, while driving efficiency and reducing operating costs. job.title: SENIOR DIRECTOR, COMMUNICATIONS, MARKETING, MEMBER & STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT
job.description:
• Critical internet infrastructure organisation
  • Lead reputation, communication, marketing, member and stakeholder engagement
  • Support new phase of organisational performance


About the organisation

.au Domain Administration Limited (auDA) is Australia’s country code Top Level Domain (ccTLD) administrator and self-regulatory policy body, which oversees the operation and management framework of the .au domain of the internet. auDA is a community-based not-for-profit public company limited by guarantee, with more than 6,000 members who are vital stakeholders and support auDA’s work and in meeting the changing needs of Australian internet users. auDA is endorsed by the Australian Government and has an agreement with the global Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers to manage the .au ccTLD. auDA’s role is to provide a safe, secure and operational namespace for more than 20 million Australian internet users. Under the Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018 (Cth), auDA has been declared as the entity that is critical to the administration of the Australian Domain Name System.  


About the role

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and a member of the executive team, the Senior Director, Communications, Marketing, Member & Stakeholder Engagement leads a team spanning communications, membership, events, stakeholder engagement, and brand and marketing. The role is responsible for protecting and enhancing the reputation of both auDA and .au through consistent, effective communication and stakeholder engagement across government, industry, members, media and the broader community. The Senior Director will provide strategic counsel to the CEO, Chair and Board on reputation, public affairs, member and stakeholder matters, and will oversee delivery of media relations, digital communications, publications, impactful events and membership programs. A significant priority is strengthening member and stakeholder engagement, while leading a high performing and collaborative team which is a trusted, enterprise-wide partner. The role also carries responsibility for issues management, crisis communications and reputation risk, and will support auDA's stakeholder engagement across an increasingly broad regulatory and government landscape.


About you

You are a senior communications and stakeholder engagement executive with a proven track record leading corporate affairs, public affairs, membership, stakeholder engagement and marketing functions. A background in member organisations and industry associations, as well as technology, telecommunications, internet governance or a regulated digital environment is advantageous. Your career reflects genuine breadth leading multi-function teams across communications and stakeholder strategy, member engagement growth, reputation and issues management, as well as effectively overseeing brand, marketing, advocacy and events. Possessing executive presence, you are comfortable sitting at the executive table and representing the organisation at this level internally and externally. Adept at managing complex stakeholder environments and navigating reputation risk, you thrive on fostering a culture of collaboration and enterprise-wide service across your team. Exposure to government, regulators or policy-makers is desirable, as is knowledge of data, CRM platforms and contemporary IT tools. This is an exciting C-suite opportunity to shape the voice, reputation and relationships of one of Australia's most critical organisations, and leave a lasting mark on our digital future.
